events.title: APIEx Symposium 2026 - Expert Evidence in Action: From Appointment to Impact in Arbitration and Litigation
events.venue: Singapore University of Social Sciences, 463 Clementi Road, Singapore 599494
events.outline: This event is organised by Asia Pacific Institute of Experts. Expert evidence often determines the outcome in complex disputes, yet tribunals continue to criticise how experts are selected, instructed & deployed. Poorly framed instructions, blurred independence and misaligned counsel/expert expectations undermine the strongest cases. Through keynote insights, panel discussions and mock engagements, dispute professionals explore the lifecycle of expert involvement, dissect real-world pitfalls, benchmark best practices and refine the lawyer–expert interface..

events.title: Deploying Turnaround Tools in Private Capital Disputes: Conflicts, Solutions, and Exit Strategies in the US$1.8 billion DyStar Saga
events.venue: Allen & Gledhill Auditorium (Level 30), One Marina Boulevard Singapore 018989
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore - Centre for International Law. The DyStar dispute has led to several landmark judgments of Singapore’s apex Court.  The receiver-led special situations M&A process that followed was a masterclass in high-stakes restructuring, with broader lessons for private capital disputes.  This seminar will address the tools and strategies to safeguard and realise investments, prevent or manage shareholder disputes, the tools and tactics that can be deployed to achieve favourable outcomes.

events.title: Accelerated Route to Fellowship in International Arbitration+
events.outline: The Accelerated Route to Fellowship has been designed for busy professionals who have substantial unassessed knowledge and experience of International Arbitration. The aim of the programme is to assess whether the candidate has the knowledge required to apply the principles and procedure of International Arbitration using arbitration legislation based on the UNCITRAL Model Law and Arbitration Rules and is capable of writing a reasoned and enforceable International Arbitration Award.

events.title: [WEBINAR] SIAC Academy Annual Lecture (Virtual Edition)
events.outline: International arbitration has been built around a model where awards are to be final. This design has served the system well, but its limitations have become apparent. Where disputes involve state resources, public entities or public interests, it is increasingly difficult to justify their final determination by a single tribunal, given the restricted scope for correction. Prof. Brekoulakis argues that sustainable arbitration depends on institutional design and a workable process of review.

events.title: CIL’s Dialogue with India High Commissioner Dr. Shilpak Ambule on Partners with Trust: India-Singapore Relations in a Changing World
events.venue: Lecture Theatre @ NUS, Bukit Timah Campus Block B, Level 3, 469 Bukit Timah Road, Singapore 259756
events.outline: This event is organised by NUS Centre for International Law. The 4th round of India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable, held in Singapore on 20th August 2026, underscored the commitment from both sides to forge an ever closer partnership. High Commissioner Dr. Ambule will share his thoughts on how India and Singapore are strengthening cooperation, expanding collaboration and leveraging their respective strengths and complimentarities, for the benefit of the two countries, within the framework of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Navigating Trade, Sustainability and Investment Law in the Era of Economic Security
events.outline: This seminar examines how sustainability, investment, economic security, and technological change are reshaping international economic law and legal practice.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Best practices for using AI tools for financial document review
events.outline: This event is organised by A.B. Maximus & Co. Pte Ltd. The Guide for Using Generative AI in the Legal Sector provides guidance for contract and document reviews. This webinar dives into the AI tools to use when the document is of a financial nature. The lawyers on the panel will share how they analyse financial statements for litigation and transactions work. Accountant and AI engineer Andrew will provide insights on the AI tools for financial and other analyses of financial statements for, inter alia, detecting discrepancies and fraud.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Navigating Issues in Bankruptcy Proceedings Including Asset Recovery and Clawbacks under the IRDA
events.outline: This seminar explores asset recovery in personal insolvency under the IRDA, including jointly owned property, matrimonial asset distributions, transactions at an undervalue and unfair preferences. It examines key procedural and substantive issues in bankruptcy proceedings, drawing on recent Singapore decisions to explain how courts balance creditors’ interests against those of affected parties and the implications for practitioners and trustees.

events.title: [WEBINAR] The Lawyer-Client Relationship: Everyday Ethical Dilemmas
events.outline: The lawyer-client relationship presents ethical challenges at every stage of a retainer, from client onboarding and due diligence, to acting on instructions, charging fees, and ultimately bringing the engagement to an end. Drawing on the practical guidance and illustrations in Chapters 2, 3, 6 and 8 of Professional Ethics Digest 2026 (published by the Law Society in July 2026), this webinar will explore everyday dilemmas faced by practitioners.

events.title: [WEBINAR] Global and Regional AI Governance and Regulation, and the Role of Data Protection in AI
events.outline: In this 2-hour webinar, participants will be exposed to: (a) an overview of AI governance and regulation and some of the key considerations that shape it; (b) A comparative scan of AI regulatory approaches in five regions, namely US, EU, China, the rest of APAC and Singapore, as well as takeaways for Singapore; and (c) The use of data protection law as a regulatory tool for AI (especially generative AI).

events.title: LawNet Training Workshop (9 December 2026)
events.venue: SAL Premises, Level 7, The Adelphi #07-01, Singapore 179803
events.outline: This training workshop guides attendees through the new features and functionalities of LawNet.com. Through walkthroughs and hands-on exercises, participants will learn how to use the revamped platform efficiently

events.title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly of Artificial Intelligence: Governance and Liability+
events.venue: Wee Chong Jin Moot Court, National University of Singapore, Faculty of Law, 16 College Avenue West Singapore 138527
events.organiser: National University of Singapore Faculty of Law
events.outline: AI offers significant benefits across sectors but also raises complex ethical, governance, and liability challenges. This 2-day conference brings together academic and industry experts to examine how governance, liability frameworks can promote responsible and fair AI. It explores global and national approaches, the application of existing and new legal principles, and appropriate remedies when AI-enabled products or services cause harm, emphasising the need for multi-stakeholder collaboration.

events.title: [WEBINAR] The Role of the United Nations in Global AI Governance
events.outline: This event is organised by National University of Singapore - Centre for International Law. The UNESCO Chair on AI Law and Sustainability at NUS’ Centre for International Law invites you to a webinar exploring the UN’s role in global AI governance. The discussion will cover international cooperation, scientific assessment, human rights, sustainable development, AI accountability, incident reporting and cross-border collaboration, including the role of civil society and countries with limited technical resources. The session concludes with a moderated discussion and audience Q&A.

events.title: [WEBINAR] E154: Anti-Money Laundering / Combating The Financing Of Terrorism (“AML / CFT”) Course
events.outline: This event is organised by Institute of Singapore Chartered Accountants (ISCA). The course is designed to enable RFAs to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of AML/CFT legislations, regulatory trends and developments in Singapore, knowledge and understanding of the AML/CFT environment in Singapore and international trends and typologies, knowledge and understanding of how to carry out risk assessment and conduct various types of customer due diligence, familiarity with ACRA Guidelines for RFAs and awareness of how ACRA’s Compliance review and inspections impact RFAs.
